issues.description: Function 'setup_env': the problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 21-22) instructs students to call setup_env() with no parameters. The reference solution (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm) declares extern setup_env (line 8) but calls it after pushing a value (push 1 at line 13, call setup_env at line 14), which implies a one-parameter signature. This contradiction between the documented no-argument call and the solution's one-argument call can confuse students about the expected signature and how to compile/run their submission.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the expected setup_env signature consistent across all artifacts. Two viable options: (A) If setup_env is meant to be no-argument: update the solution to remove the pushed argument (delete the 'push 1' at solution_repository/helloWorld.asm line 13) and keep 'call setup_env' as a no-arg call; add 'extern setup_env' to the template (near extern printf) so students can compile. Update the problem text only to clarify a no-arg call if needed. (B) If setup_env requires one integer parameter: update the problem statement to instruct students to push an integer before calling setup_env, and update the template to declare 'extern setup_env' (near extern printf) and show the push+call example. Ensure all three artifacts (problem statement, template, solution) consistently document the same calling convention and show matching example lines.
